:::{#rem-matmul-not-commutative}
#### Matrix multiplication is not commutative

The product $\matr{A}\matr{B}$ is defined only when
the number of columns of $\matr{A}$ equals the number of rows of $\matr{B}$.
Even when $\matr{A}\matr{B}$ and $\matr{B}\matr{A}$ are both defined,
they are usually different.
For example, with

$$
\matr{A} = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 \end{bmatrix},
\qquad
\matr{B} = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 0 \\ 1 & 1 \end{bmatrix},
$$

$$
\matr{A}\matr{B} = \begin{bmatrix} 3 & 2 \\ 1 & 1 \end{bmatrix}
\neq
\begin{bmatrix} 1 & 2 \\ 1 & 3 \end{bmatrix} = \matr{B}\matr{A}.
$$

:::
